from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        lecture_lines = [

        path = Arc(radius=1, start_angle=0, angle=0, color="#FF5733")

        self.place_at_grid(wave_line, 'E4')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(circle), Write(label_circle))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(point_p), Write(label_p))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF5733")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Create(path), Rotate(point_p, angle=2*PI, about_point=circle.get_center(), rate_func=linear))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF5733")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(Create(line_proj))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#33FF57")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(Create(wave_line))
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#33FF57")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The heat equation models thermal diffusion.",
            "Temperature distributes along the metal rod.",
            "Natural modes decay over time."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Bridging to the Heat Equation", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        # Animation 1
        func_u = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(np.pi * x) + 0.2 * np.sin(3 * np.pi * x), x_range=[-1, 1], color="#FFFFFF")
        
        # Animation 2
        heat_label = Text("Heat Flow", font_size=20, color="#E67E22")
        equation = MathTex(r"\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = \alpha \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}", color="#E67E22")
        
        # Animation 3
        diffusion_label = Text("Diffusion", font_size=20, color="#3498DB")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_in_area(func_u, "A2", "C5")
        self.play(Create(func_u))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#E67E22"))
        self.place_at_grid(equation, "D3")
        self.place_at_grid(heat_label, "E3")
        self.play(Write(equation), Write(heat_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#3498DB"))
        self.place_at_grid(diffusion_label, "F3")
        self.play(Write(diffusion_label))
        
        # Animate function flattening
        target_func = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.2 * np.sin(np.pi * x), x_range=[-1, 1], color="#3498DB")
        self.play(Transform(func_u, target_func))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Circles generate waves, forming Fourier series.",
            "Series solve complex heat diffusion problems.",
            "Heat flow acts as frequency harmonics."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Synthesis", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display unit circle connected to sine waves
        circle = Circle(radius=0.5, color=WHITE)
        wave = FunctionGraph(lambda t: 0.3 * np.sin(4 * PI * t), x_range=[-1, 1], color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(wave, 'B4', scale_factor=1.0)
        label1 = Text("Waves", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label1, 'C2')
        
        self.play(Create(circle), Create(wave), Write(label1))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show transition to heat equation components
        heat_graph = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.1, color="#3498DB").move_to(self.grid[f'E{i}']) for i in range(2, 6)])
        label2 = Text("Heat", font_size=20, color="#3498DB")
        self.place_at_grid(label2, 'E1')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(heat_graph), Write(label2))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#3498DB"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Summarize the synthesis of frequency in space
        conclusion = Text("Conclusion", font_size=24, color="#F1C40F")
        self.place_at_grid(conclusion, 'F3')
        
        self.play(Write(conclusion))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#F1C40F"))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Rhythm of Heat: From Circles to Fourier Series

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Geometry of Oscillation
sections.content: Establish the fundamental connection between uniform circular motion and sine/cosine waves. Use a visual 'shadow' projection where a point rotating on a circle creates a perfect sine wave on a time-axis graph.
sections.example: A 'Robot Dog' walking in a circle; its shadow cast on a wall traces a perfect wave, representing the simplest harmonic oscillation.

sections.title: Fourier's Core Concept: Building Complexity
sections.content: Explain the Principle of Superposition: any periodic function can be reconstructed by summing simple sine and cosine waves of different frequencies. Introduce the 'Epicycle' visualization where rotating gears of varying sizes stack to trace a complex shape.
sections.example: Stacking three gears of different speeds to transform a simple circular motion into the complex silhouette of a cat's profile.

sections.title: Bridging to the Heat Equation
sections.content: Introduce the Heat Equation: a Partial Differential Equation (PDE) describing how temperature diffuses over time. Explain that the Heat Equation has 'natural modes' of decay, which are sine/cosine functions. Thus, solving heat flow is equivalent to decomposing the initial temperature distribution into Fourier components.
sections.example: A metal rod with a 'zig-zag' temperature distribution; as time passes, the Fourier components decay at different speeds, 'smoothing out' the rod's temperature.

sections.title: Application: Thermal Diffusion in a Ring
sections.content: Connect the linear heat equation to circular representations. By wrapping the rod into a ring (periodic boundary conditions), the Fourier series naturally emerges as the unique way to track heat flowing around the circle.
sections.example: A circular 'Smart Heating Coil' inside an oven; the heat stabilizes into a smooth gradient, mathematically described by the sum of its Fourier modes.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis
sections.content: Recap the logical chain: Circles produce Waves -> Waves combine into Series -> Series solve the Heat Equation -> Heat flow behaves like a symphony of decaying frequencies.
sections.example: A visualization showing a complex thermal map on a circular sensor being 'unpacked' into its individual frequency components (the Fourier spectrum).
